title: Opening a session someone holds the lease on — refused one way, and a release the other

expect.why: The lease is granted. Everything below is about what may happen to it while it is held.

A worker may not open a session out from under the operator holding its lease. `open` means everyone may type, so honouring this would end the exclusivity the lease exists to provide while its holder still believed they had it — lease still valid, heartbeats still answered, and no way to observe that anyone can now type alongside them. 409 rather than 403: the request conflicts with the state the session is in, and would be fine once the lease is gone.

equals.error: Cannot switch to open while hijack is active.

expect.why: The message names the lease as the obstacle, so a worker reconnecting into a hijacked session can tell this apart from being unauthorized or unknown.
The refusal left the lease alone. A guard that refused the mode change but disturbed the lease would fail the holder just as badly and more confusingly.
And it is still exclusive. This is the assertion that catches a port whose guard returns a refusal while writing the mode anyway — the refusal alone proves what was answered, not what was stored.

The session route is deliberately not the worker route. An operator opening a session is entitled to take it back from whoever holds the lease — that is the arbitration this product exists for — so this succeeds where the worker's own attempt was refused. Two routes onto one field, and what separates them is authority, not mechanism.
It really changed, rather than being accepted and ignored.

And the lease is gone rather than merely bypassed: opening the session force-releases it, so the holder's next heartbeat finds nothing. That is the honest answer — a lease left alive while the session accepted everyone's input would tell its holder they still had something they did not.
